'''Yuga Shrine Hongū''' ({{lang|ja|由加神社本宮}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located on [[Yuga Mountain]] in the Kojima area of southern {{ill|Kurashiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurashiki|qq=}}, {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Prefecture|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Independent Shinto shrine|lt=Independent Shinto shrine|lt=Standalone Shrine|ja|単立神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Standalone Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q7882536|redirects to 単立|2=ja|3=単立|2=ja|3=単立|redirects to 単立|2=ja|3=単立|}} unaffiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Association of Shinto Shrines|qq=}}. Its modern status under the shrine Ranking system is a former {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qid=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q90139226|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}.

== Overview ==
Mount Yuga has been a center of {{ill|Iwakura rock|lt=Iwakura faith|ja|磐座信仰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwakura rock|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 磐座}} since ancient times. In 733 CE, the monk {{ill|Gyōki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gyōki|qq=}} enshrined an {{ill|Ekādaśamukha|en|Ekādaśamukha|qid=Q11404731|lt=Eleven-faced Kannon}} statue here, establishing a religious complex that merged Shinto and Buddhism under the name '''{{nihongo|{{ill|Yuga Daigongen|ja|瑜伽大権現|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yuga Daigongen|qq=}}|瑜伽大権現}}''' (Yuga Great Incarnation). According to the history of {{ill|Kumano Shrine (Kurashiki)|lt=Kumano Shrine|ja|熊野神社 (倉敷市林)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shrine (Kurashiki)|qq=}}, five disciples of {{ill|En no Gyōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/En no Gyōja|qq=}}, a prominent ascetic, brought Kumano deities from {{ill|Kii Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Province|qq=}} and established Kumano Shrine in the northern foothills of Mount Yuga. They later founded Nachi Shrine on Mount Yuga as one of the "New Kumano Three Mountains."

From the mid-{{ill|Edo period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Edo period|qq=}}, the shrine became a place of worship for the {{ill|Ikeda clan|en|Ikeda clan|qid=Q2975277|lt=Ikeda clan}}, rulers of {{ill|Bizen Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizen Province|qq=}}. The Ikeda clan sponsored the construction of the shrine’s buildings and nearby {{ill|Yugasan Rendaiji|lt=Rendaiji|ja|蓮台寺_(倉敷市)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yugasan Rendaiji|qq=}}.

The shrine is located in a bustling {{ill|Monzen-machi|ja|門前町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monzen-machi|qq=}}, with numerous souvenir shops and food stalls. During the New Year period, the shrine attracts many visitors. A specialty of Mount Yuga is the locally famous "ankoro mochi" (sweet red bean rice cakes).

In the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinbutsu bunri|qq=}} (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) policy split Yuga Shrine from Rendaiji Temple. Yuga Shrine now has 52 branch shrines across western Japan.

After {{ill|World War II|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/World War II|qq=}}, the shrine and temple informally resumed cooperation, with temple monks conducting prayers at the shrine. However, Yuga Shrine formally resumed independent religious activities in 1997, leading to a dispute with Rendaiji over property and operations.

In the Edo period, a practice known as "dual pilgrimage" emerged, encouraging worshippers to visit both {{ill|Yuga Daigongen|ja|瑜伽大権現|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yuga Daigongen|qq=}} and {{ill|Konpira Gongen|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konpira Gongen|qq=}} in {{ill|Sanuki Province|en|Sanuki Province|qid=Q929682|lt=Sanuki Province}}.
== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines Hikosa no Oshinomikoto, Kamunaobi-no-Kami, Daigongen (Honji Buddha: {{ill|Amitābha|en|Amitābha|qid=Q236242|lt=Amitābha}}, {{ill|Bhaisajyaguru|en|Bhaisajyaguru|qid=Q854773|lt=Yakushi Nyorai Medicine Buddha}}), and others, including:
* {{ill|Hikosachi no Mikoto|lt=Hikosachi no Mikoto|lt=Hikosa-no-Oshinomikoto|ja|彦狭知命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikosa-no-Oshinomikoto|qq=}}
* {{ill|Kamuna'obi|ja|神直日神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamunaobi-no-Kami|qq=}}
* {{ill|Yuga Daigongen|ja|瑜伽大権現|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yuga Daigongen|qq=}} (associated Buddhas: {{ill|Amitābha|en|Amitābha|qid=Q236242|lt=Amitābha}}, {{ill|Bhaisajyaguru|en|Bhaisajyaguru|qid=Q854773|lt=Yakushi Nyorai Medicine Buddha}})
* {{ill|Sanuki Inbe clan|ja|手置帆負命|lt=Teokihobufu no Mikoto|2=ja|3=讃岐忌部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Teokihobufu no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanuki Inbe clan|qq=}} 
* {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|Ame-no-Minakanushi|qid=Q2842779|lt=Ame-no-Minakanushi}}
* {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞鳴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}}
* {{ill|Ukanomitama|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama-no-Kami|ja|倉稲魂命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ukanomitama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ウカノミタマ}}
* {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q382005}}
* {{ill|Watatsumi|lt=Watatsumi-no-Mikoto|ja|大綿津見命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Watatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}

== Cultural Properties ==
* '''main hall''' – Built in the early Edo period, it is designated as an {{ill|Important Cultural Property of Okayama Prefecture|ja|岡山県指定重要文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property of Okayama Prefecture|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (1961).<ref name=岡山県文>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=174 |title=main hall of Yuga Shrine |publisher=Okayama Prefecture |accessdate=2018-06-24}}</ref>

== Access ==
* '''By Car:''' About 15 minutes from [[:en:Seto-Chuo Expressway|Seto-Chuo Expressway]]'s {{ill|Mizushima Interchange|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mizushima Interchange|qq=}}.
* '''By Taxi:''' About 15 minutes from {{ill|Kojima Station|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kojima Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|Seto-Ohashi Line|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seto-Ohashi Line|qq=}}.
* '''By Bus:''' A limited {{ill|Shimoden Bus|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimoden Bus|qq=}} service runs from Kojima Station to Yuga Shrine (twice daily). However, buses do not operate on weekends, holidays, or during the New Year period.
